what_was_done: The settle-held 'starting' wait in _held_answer is gone; it hands to _wait_for_running, which now decides every poll the way the rest of the held-state code does. A fresh 'running' record is answered only when its group lives and its commit equals this call's head; at another commit stop_products(subject) runs and None sends the caller to take the lock and start, so the old commit's product is replaced instead of answered (D14). On each poll a 'starting' record whose settle lock has come free is a settling start call that died: the orphan product it left holding the lock is stopped by the pid the locked body wrote, and None takes over - the loop no longer waits out _STARTING_WAIT on a dead settler. A freed product lock returns None, and the timeout keeps the settling error. The shared wait is also reached by the running branch (a record whose group is gone) and by the recordless holder of fix-4-C1-2, so one decision procedure covers every held state. Two tests added to test_env.py: test_start_replaces_a_start_in_flight_at_another_commit (two concurrent starts, env._head monkeypatched per thread to aaaa and bbbb: the second returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT with a new pid, the record at bbbb and the first product dead; pre-fix it returned the first call's pid with the record still at aaaa) and test_start_takes_over_when_the_settling_start_call_dies (a helper process killed 0.3 s into a second start's join of the settle wait: the second returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT with a new pid, the orphan dead and the record running; pre-fix it returned 1 'still settling' after 5.1 s with the orphan alive). Both fail against the pre-fix code and pass with it restored.

_held_answer's last branch - a held product lock with no usable record - no longer returns None for start()'s single lock re-probe to turn into exit 1 'the product lock stays held'. It goes to _wait_for_running like a start in flight: a 'running' record whose group lives is answered at the same commit and replaced at another, a 'starting' record appearing under a held settle lock is waited on the same way, a freed lock returns None to the caller, and a holder that never writes fails only after _STARTING_WAIT (a holder that escaped its group then costs the five seconds rather than an instant failure, as the resolution accepts). The stale-record stop the old tail performed is the waiter's dead-settler branch now, reached whenever a record turns up under a freed settle lock. Tests A and C in test_env.py, each at the head commit and at another: _overlapping_start_yet_to_write behind test_start_waits_for_a_start_yet_to_write_its_record and test_start_replaces_a_start_yet_to_write_its_record_at_another_commit (a first start holds the lock inside a delayed _launch with no record written; the overlapping start returns 0 with the same pid at the head commit, and with a new pid, the record at the new commit and the first product gone at another; pre-fix the second returned 1 'the product lock stays held' at once) and test_start_waits_out_a_recordless_holder (a holder that takes the lock for 0.5 s writing nothing: the start returns 0 well inside _STARTING_WAIT, both legs; pre-fix 1 in hundredths of a second). The case comment above the held-state tests now states cases 1 and 5 as they are tested. All four fail against the pre-fix code and pass with it restored.
